turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a laundry and dry cleaners, and lately... it's just getting out of hand. The tickets, the receipts, my workshop notes, and the actual customer jobs all just end up piled together. It gets to the point where I look at the mess and I just do not know what to handle first.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot keep their work in order and struggle to know what to handle first due to everything being piled together.

turns.doctor_question: Have you always had trouble staying organized and keeping track of tasks like this since you were younger, or is this something that's changed recently compared to how you used to function?
turns.patient_response: No, it's not really a new thing. I've pretty much always been this way. Um... even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother that I was a bright kid, but just really scattered. I was always talking out of turn, losing my papers, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my work. So, yeah, it's always been like this for me.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient notes that teachers constantly had to give them reminders just to finish their schoolwork.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient confirms they have always had trouble staying organized and describes themselves as having been 'really scattered' since grade school.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly mentions a history of 'losing my papers' in school.
symptom_reasoning.S018: The patient states they were 'always talking out of turn,' which indicates interrupting or intruding in conversations or class.

turns.doctor_question: Growing up, did you also tend to be very restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or act impulsively—like blurting things out or making quick decisions without thinking them through?
turns.patient_response: Um, I'm not really sure about the restless part. I mean, I know I talked out of turn a lot, like I just mentioned, but I don't really remember having a lot of trouble sitting still or... or making quick decisions without thinking. If I did, I guess I just didn't notice it, or maybe nobody made a big deal out of it compared to me losing my papers all the time. I mostly just remember them saying I was scattered.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly mentions 'losing my papers all the time'.
symptom_reasoning.S016: The patient confirms they 'talked out of turn a lot', aligning with blurting things out.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient states they 'don't really remember having a lot of trouble sitting still'.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient says they are 'not really sure about the restless part' and do not recall experiencing it.

turns.doctor_question: Besides your struggles at work, do you notice this same kind of disorganization and difficulty focusing in other parts of your life right now—like at home, managing finances, or in personal relationships?
turns.patient_response:
Well, at the shop it's definitely causing real issues. Because of the mess, we've had late orders, the billing gets all confused, and... honestly, it leads to some pretty tense moments with the rest of the staff and the customers. 

And outside of work... yeah, it happens there, too. Like at my church. I actually had to step back from leading some of the planning we do there. I just couldn't keep it all straight, and people were getting frustrated with me.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions that 'billing gets all confused,' implying careless mistakes and inattention to detail in their work tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes a 'mess' at work and an inability to 'keep it all straight' when planning at church, indicating clear difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
